standards.name: RFC 10008 — The HTTP QUERY Method
standards.notes: Core RFC implemented in pkg/query and pkg/cache. Published June 2026.

standards.name: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
standards.notes: HTTP semantics foundation used in pkg/query (405 Allow header, method semantics).

standards.name: RFC 7234 — HTTP/1.1 Caching
standards.notes: Cache semantics implemented in pkg/cache (TTL, X-Cache, no-transform awareness).

standards.name: RFC 8288 — Web Linking (Content-Location semantics)
standards.notes: Content-Location and Location header semantics referenced in RFC 10008 §2.3 and §2.4. Not yet implemented as a separate package.

standards.name: RFC 7807 — Problem Details for HTTP APIs
standards.notes: Error responses in pkg/query could adopt application/problem+json format. Currently plain text.

standards.label: No-Vary-Search HTTP Caching Extension
standards.impact: Monitors: allows servers to declare that certain URI query string parameters do not affect cache semantics. QUERY method uses body-based cache keys (SHA-256 of body) rather than URI query params — the two mechanisms are orthogonal. No-Vary-Search affects GET/HEAD caching; QUERY caching is governed by RFC 10008 §9 body-keyed cache. Worth tracking in case HTTPbis extends this to QUERY-method cache behaviour.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: not-applicable to current implementation. URI query params are irrelevant to QUERY's body-keyed caching. Monitor for any RFC 10008 interaction notes in later revisions. 2026-08-29: updated last_known_rev 07→09.

standards.label: Template-Driven HTTP CONNECT Proxying for TCP
standards.impact: TCP tunnelling via HTTP CONNECT. No intersection with QUERY method semantics (safe, idempotent, cacheable request with body). Not applicable.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: not-applicable. TCP proxy tunnelling is entirely orthogonal to QUERY method semantics. 2026-08-29: updated last_known_rev 12→13.

standards.label: Incremental Forwarding of HTTP Messages
standards.impact: Defines an Incremental HTTP header field instructing intermediaries to forward messages incrementally (streaming). QUERY responses could be large (DB result sets), but RFC 10008 does not define streaming semantics and pkg/query returns complete responses. Not applicable to current scope.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: not-applicable. Intermediary streaming is orthogonal to QUERY method definition. Could revisit if a streaming QUERY variant is explored.

standards.label: Perfect Forward Secrecy Extension to Oblivious HTTP
standards.impact: Oblivious HTTP extension for forward secrecy. Privacy/transport layer, no intersection with QUERY method semantics. Not applicable.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: not-applicable. Privacy transport extension unrelated to QUERY method.

standards.label: HTTP Signature Keys
standards.impact: HTTP header fields for distributing public keys used with HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421). Authentication/integrity layer — no intersection with QUERY method caching, body semantics, or safe/idempotent properties. Not applicable.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: not-applicable. Key distribution for HTTP signatures is orthogonal to QUERY method semantics.

standards.label: Unencoded Content Digest for HTTP
standards.impact: MONITORING — defines a Repr-Digest header expressing content digests over unencoded (pre-Content-Encoding) representations. Potentially relevant to QUERY body integrity: a client could include Repr-Digest over the QUERY request body so the server can verify body integrity before cache-key computation. RFC 10008 does not mandate body integrity checking, but it is a natural hardening of the body-keyed cache model. Worth tracking for any future alignment with body-keyed cache key security.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: assessed. Not currently applicable — RFC 10008 cache key uses SHA-256 of the raw body directly; no separate Repr-Digest requirement. Monitor for HTTPbis guidance on integrating Repr-Digest into the QUERY body-key computation.

standards.label: draft-ferro-httpbis-apertoid-sig (all revisions)
standards.impact: HTTP message signature extension — no intersection with QUERY method semantics.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: dismissed. Versions -00, -01, -02 all consolidated into this single not-applicable entry. Authentication/integrity layer orthogonal to QUERY.

standards.label: draft-rajappa-httpbis-connection-contamination (all revisions)
standards.impact: TCP connection contamination security analysis — no intersection with QUERY method semantics.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: dismissed. Versions -00 through -05 consolidated. HTTP connection security is orthogonal to QUERY safe/idempotent/cacheable semantics.

standards.label: draft-rosomakho-httpbis-h3-unbound-data (all revisions)
standards.impact: HTTP/3 unbound data streams — transport layer, no intersection with QUERY method semantics.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: dismissed. Versions -00, -02 consolidated. HTTP/3 transport extension orthogonal to QUERY.

standards.label: HTTP State Management Mechanism (Cookies bis)
standards.impact: Cookie semantics update — no intersection with QUERY method.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: dismissed. Cookie state management is unrelated to QUERY safe/idempotent/cacheable semantics.

standards.label: Secondary Certificate Authentication of HTTP Servers
standards.impact: TLS secondary certificate authentication — no intersection with QUERY method semantics.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: dismissed. TLS-layer authentication is orthogonal to QUERY.

ecosystem_adoption._comment: Server-side and framework QUERY support tracking. Updated manually when implementations ship.

entries.name: Apache Tomcat 12
entries.status_detail: QUERY method added to HttpServlet doXxx dispatch table (doQuery() override) via apache/tomcat#1026, merged July 1, 2026. Requires Servlet 6.1 API. Tomcat 12.0.x is the minimum version.
entries.notes: First major Java servlet container to ship native QUERY method support. Override doQuery(HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse) in a Servlet 6.1 HttpServlet subclass — no RequestMethod.valueOf workaround needed.

entries.name: Spring Framework MVC
entries.status_detail: Spring Framework GitHub issue #36988 (add first-class @QueryMapping annotation) closed as 'not planned' / duplicate. Root cause: @QueryMapping is already claimed by Spring GraphQL — using the same annotation name for Spring MVC would create an irresolvable conflict. No dedicated annotation is planned.
entries.workaround: @RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.valueOf("QUERY")) — this is the community-endorsed and Spring-team-confirmed workaround. The existing demo code at demo/index.html (Java panels) already implements this correctly. RestClient.create().method(HttpMethod.valueOf("QUERY")) on the client side.
entries.notes: The workaround is stable, correct, and already in use in this demo. No breaking change is expected — Spring MVC's RequestMethod resolution is fully extensible for non-standard HTTP methods.

entries.name: Web Browsers (Fetch API / XMLHttpRequest)
entries.status_detail: No browser vendor has shipped Fetch API or XMLHttpRequest support for QUERY method as of 2026-08-29. Browser security model (CORS preflight for non-simple methods) means QUERY would require explicit server Allow header support. Under evaluation — no public timeline.
entries.notes: QUERY from a browser would require the server to include 'QUERY' in Access-Control-Allow-Methods. The safe+idempotent semantics are browser-friendly but no vendor has prioritised implementation.
